summary: The Westminster Confession, which the Presbyterian Church in America holds as a doctrinal standard, teaches that God freely justifies those he effectually calls, not by putting righteousness in them but by pardoning their sins and counting them righteous for Christ's sake alone, through Christ's obedience and satisfaction credited to them as they receive and rest on him by faith. Faith is the alone instrument of justification, though it is never alone in the person justified. By God's eternal decree some are predestinated to everlasting life and others foreordained to everlasting death; those chosen to life were chosen before the world began, without any foreseen faith or good works, and the rest God passed by. Those whom God has accepted and sanctified cannot totally or finally fall away but will persevere to the end.

points.question: How is a person justified?
points.answer: Freely, by God's pardon and by his counting the person righteous, for Christ's sake alone, by crediting Christ's obedience and satisfaction to them; faith, itself the gift of God, is the alone instrument, yet is always accompanied by other graces and works by love.

points.question: Did God choose who would be saved?
points.answer: Yes. Some are predestinated to everlasting life and others foreordained to everlasting death. Those chosen to life were chosen in Christ before the world began, out of mere free grace, without any foreseeing of faith, good works or perseverance; the rest God passed by and ordained to dishonor and wrath for their sin.

points.question: Can salvation be lost?
points.answer: No. Those whom God has accepted in his Beloved, effectually called and sanctified, can neither totally nor finally fall away from the state of grace but will persevere to the end and be eternally saved.
